subject: Pilot success criteria, contractual sentinels & test harness
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hughes <claire@healthsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot success criteria, contractual sentinels & test harness

Claire —

Thanks again for taking the call today. As discussed, attached is a draft mutual action plan (MAP_v1.xlsx) and an initial acceptance-test matrix. I wanted to capture the success criteria and the "contractual sentinels" we talked about so there is no ambiguity at handoff. High-level asks below: 

- Acceptance tests (what passes the pilot):
  - Accuracy / Concordance: >= 92% on the 2,000-case sample set (ground-truth annotated by HealthSync SMEs)
  - Latency: P95 generation time <= 220ms for on-prem inference (dataset distribution attached)
  - Cost/throughput: Sustained 50 qps with 5% tail above baseline when batched as recommended
  - Safety/compliance: All outputs must pass the redaction rule set and produce no PHI leaks in the sample traces

- Exit gates (automatic fail/rollback triggers):
  - Any single-day regression >6 percentage points in agreement rate vs baseline
  - More than two production incidents in a 7-day window related to model hallucination or PHI exposure
  - Failure to provide SOC2 evidence requested by payer contracts within the 10-business-day window

- Contractual sentinels (contract-language asks to include with pilot SOW):
  - 30-day remediation period for quality regressions before escalation to credits
  - Canary rollback policy: automatic fallback to the latest verified checkpoint when P95 latency exceeds target for 3 consecutive hours
  - Data-retention & deletion clause aligned to HealthSync's policy (30-day retention in preview environment)

Next steps I propose:
1) You and Jordan confirm the listed thresholds or suggest alternate numbers by EOD Thursday.
2) HealthSync sends back the annotated 2k sample and any redaction rules (we can sign the mutual NDA addendum if needed).
3) We lock the MAP and convert to a DocuSign SOW (Ben will run the contract language for sentinels).

Attachment: MAP_v1.xlsx (outline of milestones, success flags, and owners)

Cheers,

Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

--
Note: attachment stub: MAP_v1.xlsx (rows: milestones; columns: owner, due, acceptance_criteria)

From: Claire Hughes <claire@healthsync.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@healthsync.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot success criteria, contractual sentinels & test harness

Mina —

Thanks for the clear write-up. This is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our end: 

1) The 92% concordance target is reasonable, but we want a secondary metric: F1 on the critical-label subset (n=400) >= 0.88. Can you add that to the acceptance matrix?
2) Latency target: HealthSync will run the on-prem instance in a constrained zone — can we relax P95 to <= 300ms for the first 2 weeks while we warm caches? After warmup we expect P95 <= 220ms.
3) For the SOC2 evidence, our legal team will need an exported audit log for the pilot window (not just summary). Is Redwood able to provide per-token audit trails?

I attached our preliminary acceptance test sample (acceptance-tests.csv) with notes on which cases are high-risk. Also looping Jordan to confirm timelines — we are aiming to conclude the pilot and have a commercial decision by 2026-10-01.

On the sentinels: the 30-day remediation window is acceptable. We will ask procurement to include a milestone-based payment tied to the MAP milestones.

I'll review the MAP worksheet and propose minor edits inline.

Best,

Claire Hughes
Director, Integrations | HealthSync
claire@healthsync.com

--
attachment stub: acceptance-tests.csv (400 high-risk IDs + 1600 random sample, columns: id,label,notes)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot success criteria, contractual sentinels & test harness

Mina / Marissa —

Forwarding Claire's note. Quick internal summary / proposed updates: 

- Add F1 >= 0.88 on the 400-case high-risk subset as a secondary pass metric.
- Update the latency fallback: include an explicit "warmup window" (first 48 hours) where P95 <= 300ms is tol'erd. Post-warmup we require <= 220ms. This aligns with their infra note.
- Audit logs: engineering can provide per-token traces for the pilot (redacted as needed). Ops will need an HMAC-signed export; I'll ask infra to confirm turnaround (target 5 business days).
- Contract language: propose a milestone payment schedule tied to: MAP milestone 2 (evidence delivery) and MAP milestone 4 (pilot signoff). Also include a clause: "If regression >6pp persists beyond remediation window, Redwood will credit 10% of pilot fees for each additional week until resolved" — placeholder to share with legal.

I suggest we schedule a 30-minute signoff call Thursday 2pm PT to walk HealthSync through the updated acceptance matrix and the remediation flow. Mina, can you propose a calendar slot? I'll draft the DocuSign SOW template and loop in legal once Claire signs off on thresholds.

Cheers,
Ben
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference
